key_insight: Decoded quantum interferometry can solve a streaming polynomial-interpolation problem with provable polylog-memory quantum efficiency, while matching classical performance requires polynomial space.
engineering_relevance: The result suggests quantum streaming and fault-tolerant memory-constrained systems may offer real resource advantages when input size and qubit overhead dominate.
method: Generalize optimal polynomial intersection using Hermite interpolation and Hasse derivatives.
Adapt the DQI algorithm to stream over the input in one pass with polylogarithmic memory and per-item processing time.
Compare against classical streaming algorithms under multi-pass and unbounded-time conditions to establish lower-space hardness.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a quantum algorithm achieving 93% of constraints with one pass and polylog space, versus a classical lower bound showing 76% satisfaction already needs polynomial space.
watch_item: The quantum advantage is shown in a streaming/interpolation setting, so practical deployment still depends on fault-tolerant implementation overhead and whether the model matches real-world data streams.
paper_title: Exponential quantum advantages for decoded quantum interferometry in the streaming setting
